SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Progressive numbness, tingling, and perceived weakness in left upper extremity (elbow to hand) with palmar involvement of 2nd–4th digits; onset ≈ 2 weeks ago after starting a boxing class; not relieved by massage, warm baths, or ibuprofen.
- Associated/episodic symptoms:
  • Occasional left shoulder discomfort during movement.  
  • Single episode of transient peripheral visual loss in left eye ≈ 20 minutes, a few weeks ago.  
  • Intermittent fatigue-related headaches.  
  • Recent upper-respiratory illness (“bad cold/flu”) one month ago.
- Denies seizures, loss of consciousness, lower-extremity weakness. Neck pain response contradictory (see Quality checks).
- Past medical history: None reported.
- Previous surgeries: None reported.
- Medications:
  • Ibuprofen – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Vitamin D – dose/frequency not documented.  
  • Iron supplement – taken irregularly, dose not documented.  
  • Melatonin – dose/frequency not documented.
- Social history: Regular exercise; recently started boxing class. Alcohol socially; one recent binge episode. Smoking/drug use not discussed.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
(No in-clinic examination performed; video consult only.)
- No vitals recorded.
- No documented neurologic or musculoskeletal exam findings.
- Investigations to date: None.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left upper-limb numbness/weakness
   - Assessment: Suspected central or peripheral neurologic etiology; multiple sclerosis (MS) noted as a serious consideration.
   - Differential diagnosis: Cervical radiculopathy, peripheral neuropathy/entrapment, post-viral neuritis, demyelinating disease (e.g., MS), cerebrovascular event (TIA), overuse/traumatic injury from boxing.
   - Investigations planned: Urgent neurology evaluation with brain MRI (± spinal imaging) and further neurologic work-up.
   - Treatment planned: None initiated pending specialist assessment.
   - Relevant referrals: Urgent neurology referral.

2. Transient left-eye visual loss
   - Assessment: Possible optic neuritis or TIA; may be related to demyelinating disease.
   - Investigations planned: To be included in neurology work-up; imaging of optic pathway as indicated.
   - Treatment planned: None at present.

3. Patient education & safety-netting
   - Treatment/Advice: Continue current OTC analgesia only if needed. No steroids until diagnosis confirmed.
   - Red-flag instructions: Attend Emergency Department if weakness progresses (especially to legs), new or worsening headaches, vomiting, seizures, or recurrent/worsening visual symptoms.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergies, complete medication doses/frequencies, vitals, focused neurologic/physical examination findings.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient answered “Yes” then “No” regarding neck pain – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational noise but clinically adequate.
